   428→
   429→## Performance Optimizations
   430→
   431→**Optimized for M1 Pro (8 perf cores + 16GB RAM)**
   432→
   433→### Parallel Processing
   434→
   435→| Component | Setting | Description |
   436→|-----------|---------|-------------|
   437→| **PDF Workers** | `8` workers | One per performance core |
   438→| **Threads per Worker** | `2` threads | Total 16 threads = full CPU utilization |
   439→| **Item Batch Size** | `50` items | Balances memory vs throughput |
   440→| **Qdrant Batch Size** | `500` points | 5x faster writes |
   441→| **GPU Embedding Batch** | `32` chunks | Optimizes MPS GPU usage |
   442→
   443→**Total thread count**: 8 workers × 2 threads = 16 threads (matches M1 Pro's 8 perf + 2 efficiency cores)
   444→
   445→### Memory Management
   446→
   447→| Strategy | Benefit |
   448→|----------|---------|
   449→| **Quantization** | 75% RAM savings on vectors |
   450→| **Subprocess Isolation** | Prevents memory leaks from C++ crashes |
   451→| **CPU-only Parsing** | Avoids MPS GPU memory exhaustion (18GB limit) |
   452→| **Automatic Cleanup** | Removes temp files after processing |
   453→
   454→### Expected Performance
   455→
   456→| Metric | Value | Notes |
   457→|--------|-------|-------|
   458→| **Metadata-Only** | ~5-10 items/sec | Title, abstract, notes only |
   459→| **Full-Text** | ~2-5 items/sec | Includes PDF parsing with Docling |
   460→| **3425 Items** | ~35-47 hours | Full-text indexing with current config |
   461→| **Search Latency** | <100ms | Hybrid search with reranking |
   462→
   463→**Performance notes**:
   464→- CPU-only Docling is 7.3x faster than GPU mode (35s vs 254s per PDF)
   465→- GPU still used for embeddings (sequential, no contention)
   466→- Deduplication adds negligible overhead (~1ms per item)
   467→
   468→---
   469→
   470→## Critical Fixes
   471→
   472→**Production-ready improvements (October 2025)**
   473→
   474→### 1. Subprocess Isolation
   475→
   476→**Problem**: pypdfium2 C++ backend crashes bypassed Python exception handling, causing semaphore leaks and process crashes after 150-200 PDFs.
   477→
   478→**Solution**: Run Docling in isolated subprocess with configurable timeout.
   479→
   480→**Benefits**:
   481→- ✅ Main process immune to C++ crashes
   482→- ✅ Handles large documents (1-hour timeout)
   483→- ✅ Supports infinite timeout (`null`)
   484→- ✅ Clear error codes: `"failed"`, `"timeout"`, `"error"`
   485→
   486→**Implementation**: `local_db.py:_extract_text_from_pdf()`
   487→
   488→### 2. Removed pdfminer Fallback
   489→
   490→**Problem**: PDFs timing out fell back to pdfminer, resulting in inconsistent output quality:
   491→- Docling: 49 chunks × 512 tokens + rich metadata (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐)
   492→- pdfminer: 1 blob × 8000 tokens, no metadata (⭐⭐)
   493→
   494→**Solution**: Removed pdfminer fallback entirely.
   495→
   496→**Benefits**:
   497→- ✅ 100% consistent high-quality chunking
   498→- ✅ All indexed papers have identical structure
   499→- ✅ Fail loudly instead of silent degradation
   500→
   501→### 3. Configurable Timeout
   502→
   503→**Problem**: 30s timeout insufficient for large documents (textbooks, dissertations).
   504→
   505→**Solution**: Configurable timeout with sensible defaults.
   506→
   507→**Options**:
   508→- `3600` (1 hour) - Default, handles most documents
   509→- `null` - Infinite timeout for extremely large PDFs
   510→- Custom integer - Set per your needs
   511→
   512→**Configuration**: `config.json` → `semantic_search.docling.subprocess_timeout`
   513→
   514→---
   515→
   516→## Indexing Pipeline
   517→
   518→**Standard default production pipeline command:**
   519→
   520→\```bash
   521→agent-zot update-db --force-rebuild --fulltext
   522→\```
   523→
   524→### What This Does
   525→
   526→**Step-by-step execution:**
   527→
   528→1. ✅ **Delete Qdrant collection** (`--force-rebuild` flag)
   529→   - Ensures clean slate
   530→   - Removes any contaminated data
   531→
   532→2. ✅ **Read all items from local Zotero database**
   533→   - Direct SQLite access (fast)
   534→   - No API rate limits
   535→
   536→3. ✅ **Parse PDFs with Docling**
   537→   - Subprocess-isolated (crash-proof)
   538→   - 1-hour timeout per PDF
   539→   - CPU-only processing (7.3x faster)
   540→   - HybridChunker: 512 tokens per chunk
   541→   - Preserves structure + metadata
   542→
   543→4. ✅ **Generate embeddings**
   544→   - BGE-M3 dense vectors (1024D)
   545→   - BM25 sparse vectors (10,000 features)
   546→   - GPU-accelerated (batch size 32)
   547→
   548→5. ✅ **Store in Qdrant**
   549→   - Hybrid vectors (dense + sparse)
   550→   - Scalar quantization (int8)
   551→   - HNSW indexing (m=32, ef=200)
   552→   - Batch size 500 for fast writes
   553→
   554→6. ✅ **Extract Neo4j knowledge graph** (optional)
   555→   - GPT-4o-mini entity extraction
   556→   - 6 entity types, 10 relationship types
   557→   - Entity resolution enabled
   558→
   559→7. ✅ **Optimize Qdrant collection**
   560→   - Automatic after indexing
   561→   - Builds final HNSW index
   562→
   563→### Command Flags
   564→
   565→| Flag | Effect | Default |
   566→|------|--------|---------|
   567→| `--force-rebuild` | Delete collection before indexing | `false` (incremental) |
   568→| `--fulltext` | Parse PDFs with Docling | `true` (from config) |
   569→| `--limit N` | Process only N items | None (all items) |
   570→
   571→**Note**: Flags override config defaults. Without flags, uses values from `update_config`.
   572→
   573→### Monitoring Progress

   581→# Check Qdrant collection size
   582→curl http://localhost:6333/collections/zotero_library_qdrant

   670→### Docling Parsing Errors
   671→
   672→**Low text extraction** → OCR would trigger (but disabled)
   673→- Solution: Verify PDF is not scanned/image-only
   674→- Consider re-OCRing PDF externally first
   675→
   676→**Large PDFs timeout** → Increase subprocess timeout
   677→- Edit: `config.json` → `docling.subprocess_timeout`
   678→- Set to `null` for infinite timeout
   679→
   680→**Formula parsing issues** → Toggle formula enrichment
   681→- Edit: `config.json` → `docling.do_formula_enrichment`

   688→
   689→# Access Neo4j browser

   703→
   704→## Active Pipeline Components
   705→
   706→**For the complete, detailed execution path of the production indexing pipeline, see the [Active Pipeline Reference](../CLAUDE.md#active-pipeline-reference) section in CLAUDE.md.**
   707→
   708→This section provides a high-level overview of which files and directories are active in the standard production pipeline:
   709→
   710→### Standard Production Command
   711→
   712→\```bash
   713→agent-zot update-db --force-rebuild --fulltext
   714→\```
   715→
   716→### Active Execution Path
   717→
   718→**Core files used** (in order of execution):
   719→
   720→1. **CLI Entry Point**: `src/agent_zot/core/cli.py`
   721→   - Parses command-line flags
   722→   - Loads config from `~/.config/agent-zot/config.json`
   723→
   724→2. **Orchestration**: `src/agent_zot/search/semantic.py`
   725→   - Routes to appropriate indexing path
   726→   - For fulltext + local mode → delegates to `local_zotero.py`
   727→
   728→3. **Local Database Access** (MAIN ACTIVE PATH): `src/agent_zot/database/local_zotero.py`
   729→   - Direct SQLite access to Zotero database
   730→   - Parallel PDF processing (8 workers)
   731→   - **Contains correct hardcoded defaults** for all Docling settings
   732→   - **This is where the magic happens for production indexing**
   733→
   734→4. **PDF Parsing**: `src/agent_zot/parsers/docling.py`
   735→   - Runs in isolated subprocess (crash protection)
   736→   - HybridChunker with BGE-M3 tokenizer
   737→   - CPU-only processing (7.3x faster than GPU)
   738→
   739→5. **Vector Storage**: `src/agent_zot/clients/qdrant.py`
   740→   - BGE-M3 embedding generation (GPU-accelerated)
   741→   - Hybrid vectors (dense 1024D + sparse BM25)
   742→   - Batch upsert to Qdrant (batch_size=500)
   743→
   744→### Data Locations
   745→
   746→**Active storage locations**:
   747→
   748→| Location | Purpose | Required |
   749→|----------|---------|----------|
   750→| `~/.config/agent-zot/config.json` | User configuration overrides | ✅ Yes |
   751→| `~/Zotero/zotero.sqlite` | Zotero source database | ✅ Yes |
   752→| `~/toolboxes/agent-zot/qdrant_storage/` | Vector data storage | ✅ Yes |
   753→| `/tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log` | Live indexing log | ✅ Yes |
   754→
   755→### Minimal Required Configuration
   756→
   757→**Only 4 settings need to be in `config.json`** - everything else uses smart defaults:
   758→
   759→\```json
   760→{
   761→  "client_env": {
   762→    "ZOTERO_LOCAL": "true"
   763→  },
   764→  "semantic_search": {
   765→    "embedding_model": "sentence-transformers",
   766→    "sentence_transformer_model": "BAAI/bge-m3",
   767→    "collection_name": "zotero_library_qdrant"
   768→  }
   769→}
   770→\```
   771→
   772→All other settings documented in this file (Docling chunking, HNSW parameters, quantization, etc.) have correct hardcoded defaults in `local_zotero.py` and only need to be added to `config.json` if you want to override them.
   773→
   774→### Files NOT in Active Path
   775→
   776→These files exist but are NOT used for the standard production pipeline:
   777→
   778→- ❌ `src/agent_zot/parsers/pymupdf_parser.py` - Deprecated parser
   779→- ❌ `src/agent_zot/clients/chroma_client.py` - Old vector database
   780→- ❌ `src/agent_zot/clients/better_bibtex.py` - Optional, not required
   781→- ❌ `config_examples/config_chroma.json` - Old template
   782→
   783→### Why Two Code Paths?
   784→
   785→**Short answer**: `semantic.py` handles both API mode and local mode. For fulltext + local mode (our standard production pipeline), it delegates to `local_zotero.py` which has optimized parallel processing and correct defaults.
   786→
   787→**Key insight**: The DoclingParser defaults in `semantic.py:77-87` are NOT used for fulltext indexing with local mode. Instead, `local_zotero.py:265-272` provides the correct defaults via subprocess code generation.
   788→
   789→### Verification
   790→
   791→**How to verify the correct pipeline is active**:
   792→
   793→\```bash
   794→# Check config has BGE-M3
   795→grep "sentence_transformer_model" ~/.config/agent-zot/config.json
   796→
   797→# Verify BGE-M3 loading in log
   798→tail -f /tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log | grep "Load pretrained"
   799→# Should show: "BAAI/bge-m3"
   800→
   801→# Verify 1024D vectors
   802→tail -f /tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log | grep "dimension"
   803→# Should show: "dimension: 1024"
   804→
   805→# Check physical storage
   806→du -sh ~/toolboxes/agent-zot/qdrant_storage/collections/zotero_library_qdrant/
   807→\```
   808→
   809→**For complete details on the execution flow, verification points, and troubleshooting, see [CLAUDE.md - Active Pipeline Reference](../CLAUDE.md#active-pipeline-reference).**

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929)**_

Perfect! Looking at the code (qdrant.py:476-479), here's exactly how it works:

## Qdrant Storage Structure

**Each chunk is stored as a separate point** with:

1. **Vectors** (for similarity search):
   - Dense: 1024D BGE-M3 embedding
   - Sparse: BM25 keyword vector

2. **Payload** (metadata + text):
   ```python
   payload = {
       "document": batch_docs[i],  # ← THE CHUNK TEXT itself
       "item_key": "ABC123",        # Zotero item ID
       "title": "Paper Title",
       "creators": ["Author1", "Author2"],
       "year": 2023,
       "doc_type": "chunk",
       "is_chunk": true,
       "chunk_metadata": {
           "headings": ["Section 1", "Subsection A"],
           "page_num": 5,
           "hierarchy": [...]
       }
   }
   ```

## Storage Model

**No full-text assembly** - Qdrant stores:
- ✅ **Individual chunks** as separate searchable points
- ✅ **Chunk text** in the `"document"` field of each point's payload
- ✅ **All metadata** (title, authors, year, page numbers, headings)
- ❌ **NOT** the full assembled document text

## Example

For a 100-page paper parsed into 200 chunks:
- **200 separate Qdrant points** (vectors + payloads)
- Each point contains one chunk's text (~512 tokens)
- Each point links back to the same `item_key`
- Search retrieves relevant chunks, not full papers

## To Get Full Text

You would need to:
1. Query Qdrant for all chunks with `item_key = "ABC123"`
2. Sort by `page_num` or chunk order
3. Concatenate the `"document"` field from each chunk

**That's why the Neo4j population from Qdrant is viable** - you can reconstruct full document text by aggregating all chunks for each paper.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929)**_

Yes, exactly! **Each chunk is stored with BOTH representations**:

## Storage per Chunk

```
Qdrant Point {
  id: "uuid-12345",
  
  vectors: {
    dense: [0.234, -0.891, 0.445, ...],      // 1024 floats (BGE-M3 embedding)
    sparse: {indices: [42, 156, ...],         // BM25 keyword vector
             values: [0.8, 0.6, ...]}
  },
  
  payload: {
    "document": "This is the actual chunk text...",  // ← FULL TEXT stored here
    "item_key": "ABC123",
    "title": "Paper Title",
    "year": 2023,
    "chunk_metadata": {...}
  }
}
```

## Why Both?

1. **Vectors** → Fast similarity search (find relevant chunks)
2. **Text in payload** → Return actual content to user

## Search Flow

```
Query: "transformers in NLP"
  ↓
1. Convert query to vector (BGE-M3)
  ↓
2. Search Qdrant vectors (fast ANN search)
  ↓
3. Return top matches with their payloads
  ↓
4. User sees: payload["document"] = "...actual chunk text about transformers..."
```

**Without storing the text**, you'd only get vector IDs back with no way to show the user what was actually found!

## Storage Cost

For a 100-page paper → 200 chunks:
- **Vectors**: 200 × (1024 floats + sparse) ≈ 1-2 MB
- **Text**: 200 × (~512 tokens) ≈ 200-400 KB
- **Total**: ~2 MB per paper

So yes, the text is duplicated (once as embedding, once as raw text), but that's necessary for the retrieval to work.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929)**_

**Neo4j takes RAW TEXT only** (no vectors). Here's the flow:

## What Neo4j Receives (lines 350-367)

```python
full_content = "\n\n".join([
    f"Title: {title}",
    f"Authors: {', '.join(authors)}",
    f"Year: {year}",
    f"\nAbstract: {abstract}",
    "\nKey Content:",
    chunks[0],  # First 3 chunks only
    chunks[1],
    chunks[2]
])
```

**Only text**, specifically:
- Title
- Authors  
- Year
- Abstract
- First 3 chunks of full text (not all chunks!)

## What Neo4j Does With It (line 417)

```python
result = kg_builder.run_async(text=full_content)
```

1. **Sends text to Ollama Mistral 7B** (or OpenAI GPT-4o-mini)
2. **LLM extracts entities** (Person, Institution, Concept, Method, etc.)
3. **LLM identifies relationships** (AUTHORED_BY, USES_METHOD, etc.)
4. **Creates graph nodes and edges** in Neo4j

## Neo4j Can Also Generate Embeddings (line 387)

```python
embedder=self.embeddings,  # OpenAI text-embedding-3-large
```

But these are **new embeddings for the graph nodes**, not reusing Qdrant's vectors. Neo4j can embed entity names/descriptions for semantic similarity within the graph.

## Summary

| System | Input | Storage |
|--------|-------|---------|
| **Qdrant** | Raw text chunks → Generate BGE-M3 vectors | Vectors + text payloads |
| **Neo4j** | Raw text (title/abstract/3 chunks) → LLM extracts entities | Graph nodes + relationships (optional embeddings) |

**No vector reuse** - each system has its own purpose:
- Qdrant: Fast semantic search over document chunks
- Neo4j: Relationship discovery and graph traversal

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929)**_

**Use the text chunks from Qdrant - no need to re-index.** Here's why:

## Qdrant Chunks Are Perfect for Neo4j

The chunks stored in Qdrant are:
- ✅ **High-quality Docling output** (structure-preserving, clean text)
- ✅ **Already parsed and cleaned** (same quality you'd get from re-parsing)
- ✅ **Properly segmented** with metadata (headings, page numbers)
- ✅ **Complete coverage** (all text from all papers)

## Re-indexing Would Be Wasteful

Re-parsing 2,500 PDFs would:
- ❌ Take another ~8-10 hours
- ❌ Produce **identical text** (same Docling parser, same settings)
- ❌ Waste CPU/electricity for zero benefit

## Implementation Strategy

To populate Neo4j from Qdrant:

```python
# For each paper:
1. Query Qdrant: get all chunks where item_key = "ABC123"
2. Sort by page_num or chunk order
3. Take first ~10-20 chunks (enough for entity extraction)
4. Send to Neo4j add_paper_to_graph()
```

**Note**: Neo4j only uses first 3 chunks anyway (line 365), so you don't even need all chunks - just grab the first 10-20 from Qdrant.

## Only Caveat

If you had **parsing errors** during indexing (failed PDFs), you might want to re-parse only those specific papers. But for successfully indexed papers, reusing Qdrant text is the smart choice.

**Recommendation**: Write a script to populate Neo4j from Qdrant's stored chunks. Much faster than re-parsing everything.

  - Hybrid search (dense 1024D + sparse BM25)

  - Vectors AND text stored together in payload

  - Extracts 8 entity types: Person, Institution, Concept, Method, Dataset, Theory, Journal, Field

# Create points for Qdrant
points = []
for i, (doc_id, embedding, metadata) in enumerate(zip(batch_ids, embeddings, batch_metas)):
    # Add document text to metadata
    payload = dict(metadata)
    payload["document"] = batch_docs[i]  # ← THE CHUNK TEXT stored here
    
    # Store the original Zotero key in payload for retrieval
    payload["item_key"] = doc_id
    
    # Convert Zotero key to UUID for Qdrant ID
    point_id = str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS, f"zotero.{doc_id}"))
    
    if self.enable_hybrid_search and sparse_embeddings:
        # Hybrid mode: use named vectors
        points.append(PointStruct(
            id=point_id,
            vector={
                "dense": embedding,      # 1024D BGE-M3 vector
                "sparse": sparse_embeddings[i]  # BM25 sparse vector
            },
            payload=payload  # Contains "document" field with text
        ))
```

**Explanation**: Each chunk is stored as a Qdrant point with BOTH the vector representation AND the actual text in the payload. This enables returning the original text when search results are found.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL: Monitoring Long-Running Indexing Jobs

**NEVER trust log files alone. ALWAYS verify with multiple sources.**

When checking indexing status, you MUST follow this protocol:

### 1. Find the Active Log (NEVER assume)
```bash
# Get most recently modified log file
ls -lt /tmp/*.log | head -1

# Multiple log files may exist from old runs - they can mislead you!
```

### 2. Verify with Qdrant (Ground Truth)
```bash
# Check actual point count in Qdrant
curl -s http://localhost:6333/collections/zotero_library_qdrant | \
  python3 -c "import sys, json; data = json.load(sys.stdin); print(f\"Points: {data['result']['points_count']:,}\")"
```

### 3. Check Process Status
```bash
# Verify process is actually running and not stuck
ps aux | grep "agent-zot update-db" | grep -v grep
# Look for: CPU usage (should be 10-15%), process state (should not be 'S' for sleeping)
```

### 4. Cross-Reference All Three
- **Log shows progress** + **Qdrant count increasing** + **Process active** = ✅ Running correctly
- **Log stopped** + **Qdrant count static** + **Process sleeping** = ❌ Stuck/frozen
- **Log active** but **Qdrant count not matching** = ⚠️ Wrong log file

### Quick Status Script
```bash
/tmp/check-indexing-status.sh
# This script checks all sources automatically
```

### Reference File
```bash
cat /tmp/ACTIVE_INDEXING_LOG.txt
# Always check this file first to know which log is active
```

**Why this matters:** Multiple indexing runs create multiple log files. If you check the wrong log (e.g., one from a stuck/old run), you'll report incorrect progress. The user will catch your mistake and lose trust. ALWAYS verify with Qdrant's live data.
```

**Root Cause**: Multiple log files from previous indexing runs. I grabbed an old one by name pattern instead of checking which was most recently modified.

**Prevention**: Always use `ls -lt /tmp/*.log | head -1` to find ACTUAL active log, then verify against Qdrant's live data.

## 5. Problem Solving

### Solved Problem 1: Qdrant Storage Model Clarity
**Problem**: User needed to understand exactly how Qdrant stores text vs vectors

**Solution**: Explained with code evidence that each chunk is stored as a separate Qdrant point containing:
- Dense vector (1024D BGE-M3)
- Sparse vector (BM25)
- Payload with `document` field containing actual chunk text
- All metadata (title, authors, year, page numbers, headings)

**Result**: User understood that Qdrant has both vector and text, making it viable source for Neo4j population without re-parsing.

### Solved Problem 2: Neo4j Reindexing Strategy
**Problem**: Should Neo4j be populated by re-parsing PDFs or reusing Qdrant chunks?

**Solution**: Advised to reuse Qdrant chunks because:
- Same Docling parser, same settings = identical text
- Would save 8-10 hours of re-parsing
- Only need first 10-20 chunks per paper (Neo4j only uses 3)
- Can query Qdrant for all chunks by item_key and reconstruct text

**Result**: User accepted recommendation to use Qdrant text chunks.

### Solved Problem 3: Log File Confusion Crisis
**Problem**: Multiple log files from previous runs caused me to read wrong log and report incorrect status

**Solution Implemented**:
1. **Reference file**: `/tmp/ACTIVE_INDEXING_LOG.txt` - Always check this first
2. **Verification script**: `/tmp/check-indexing-status.sh` - Checks all sources automatically
3. **Mandatory protocol**: Added to CLAUDE.md as prominent warning at top
4. **3-step verification**:
   - Find active log (most recently modified)
   - Check Qdrant API (ground truth)
   - Verify process status
5. **Git commit**: Made permanent in repository

**Result**: Systematic approach to prevent future confusion. User explicitly requested this be documented so I "never ever forget."

No, the status I gave you showed **both parsing AND embedding are still ongoing simultaneously**. Here's what's actually happening:

**Pipeline Architecture:**
- Parsing and embedding happen **in parallel, not sequentially**
- The pipeline processes papers in batches of 200
- For each batch:
  1. Parse 200 PDFs → extract chunks (parallel, 8 workers)
  2. Embed those chunks → generate vectors (GPU, batch_size=32)
  3. Upload to Qdrant (batch_size=500)
  4. Move to next batch of 200 papers

**Current Status (as of my last update):**
- ✅ **1,650 papers parsed AND embedded** (out of 3,426 total)
- 🔄 **Currently embedding batch 5/6** from the most recent 200-paper batch

- ❌ NOT: "Parse all 3,426 PDFs → Then embed all chunks"
- ✅ CORRECT: "Parse 200 → Embed 200 → Upload → Parse next 200 → Embed next 200..."

      batch_items = local_items[batch_start:batch_end]
      ...
      extraction_data[item_key] = extraction_result
  ```
  This showed ALL parsing happens first, storing results in `extraction_data` dict.

### 4. **Critical Log Check**
Then I ran this command:
```bash
grep -E "(Batch.*complete|Extracted content for)" /tmp/agent-zot-production-index.log | tail -20
```

**This revealed the truth:**
```
Extracted content for 3400/3426 items (parallel with 8 workers)...
2025-10-11 22:28:25,144 - INFO - Batch 3400-3426 complete, garbage collected
```

**Key evidence:**
- Parsing completed at **22:28 yesterday** (Oct 11)
- **ALL 3,426 papers parsed** before moving to embedding
- The "Uploaded batch 4" messages I saw earlier were from the **embedding stage**, not parsing

### 5. **Realization**
The Qdrant count of 1,603 wasn't "1,603 papers processed" - it was **1,603 chunks uploaded** from the embedding stage that started AFTER all parsing finished.

## Which Logs I Checked

1. **`/tmp/agent-zot-production-index.log`** (the active log)
   - Used grep to find "Extracted content for" progress messages
   - Found "Batch complete" messages showing parsing finished
   - Saw timestamps proving parsing ended 5 hours ago

2. **Did NOT check** (initially):
   - The actual extraction completion messages
   - The timestamps showing when parsing vs embedding started

## The Lesson

I should have checked the log file more thoroughly from the beginning instead of making assumptions based on partial log output. Your skepticism was 100% justified and led me to verify with concrete evidence. Thank you for pushing back!

docs: Add pipeline stage detection protocol to CLAUDE.md

Added critical section 5 "Understanding Pipeline Stages" to document
how to determine indexing progress from log files.

## New Documentation

**Problem:** Logs don't show clear "Stage 1 Complete, Stage 2 Started"
messages, making it impossible to know if "Processing batch 5/7" refers
to parsing or embedding without searching backwards.

**Solution:** Document exact grep commands and log markers to search for:
- "Extracted content for X/Y items" = parsing progress
- "Batch complete, garbage collected" = parsing finished
- "add_documents called with XXXX documents" = embedding started
- "Processing batch X/Y (500 docs)" = embedding in progress

**Example:** Shows real log output with timestamps and annotations
explaining how to calculate stage completion percentages.

**Why it matters:** Without this protocol, progress reporting is
ambiguous and can mislead about overall completion status.

This complements the existing log file verification protocol and
ensures accurate progress tracking for long-running indexing jobs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"`

# Create points for Qdrant
points = []
for i, (doc_id, embedding, metadata) in enumerate(zip(batch_ids, embeddings, batch_metas)):

    payload = dict(metadata)
    payload["document"] = batch_docs[i]  # ← THE CHUNK TEXT stored here
    
    # Store the original Zotero key in payload for retrieval
    payload["item_key"] = doc_id
    
    # Convert Zotero key to UUID for Qdrant ID
    point_id = str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS, f"zotero.{doc_id}"))
    
    if self.enable_hybrid_search and sparse_embeddings:
        # Hybrid mode: use named vectors
        points.append(PointStruct(
            id=point_id,
            vector={
                "dense": embedding,      # 1024D BGE-M3 vector
                "sparse": sparse_embeddings[i]  # BM25 sparse vector
            },
            payload=payload  # Contains "document" field with text

max_workers = 8  # INCREASED from 7 to fully utilize 8 performance cores
max_queue_size = 16  # 2x workers prevents excessive semaphore accumulation
batch_size = 200  # INCREASED from 100: reduces batch overhead, faster overall
extracted = 0

# Process in batches to prevent semaphore accumulation
for batch_start in range(0, len(local_items), batch_size):
    batch_end = min(batch_start + batch_size, len(local_items))
    batch_items = local_items[batch_start:batch_end]
    
    logger.info(f"Processing batch {batch_start}-{batch_end} ({len(batch_items)} items) with {max_workers} workers")
    
    # Use standard ThreadPoolExecutor with as_completed()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
        # Submit all extraction tasks for this batch
        future_to_item = {executor.submit(extract_item_fulltext, it): it for it in batch_items}
        
        # Process results as they complete (natural backpressure)
        for future in as_completed(future_to_item):
            try:
                # Get the result (item_key, extraction_dict)
                item_key, extraction_result = future.result()
                extraction_data[item_key] = extraction_result
                extracted += 1
```
**Finding**: ALL papers parsed first, stored in `extraction_data` dict, THEN embedding starts

## ⚠️ CRITICAL: Monitoring Long-Running Indexing Jobs

**NEVER trust log files alone. ALWAYS verify with multiple sources.**

When checking indexing status, you MUST follow this protocol:

### 1. Find the Active Log (NEVER assume)
```bash
# Get most recently modified log file
ls -lt /tmp/*.log | head -1

# Multiple log files may exist from old runs - they can mislead you!
```

### 2. Verify with Qdrant (Ground Truth)
```bash
# Check actual point count in Qdrant
curl -s http://localhost:6333/collections/zotero_library_qdrant | \
  python3 -c "import sys, json; data = json.load(sys.stdin); print(f\"Points: {data['result']['points_count']:,}\")"
```

### 3. Check Process Status
```bash
# Verify process is actually running and not stuck
ps aux | grep "agent-zot update-db" | grep -v grep
```

### 4. Cross-Reference All Three
- **Log shows progress** + **Qdrant count increasing** + **Process active** = ✅ Running correctly
- **Log stopped** + **Qdrant count static** + **Process sleeping** = ❌ Stuck/frozen
- **Log active** but **Qdrant count not matching** = ⚠️ Wrong log file

### Quick Status Script
```bash
/tmp/check-indexing-status.sh
```

### Reference File
```bash
cat /tmp/ACTIVE_INDEXING_LOG.txt
# Always check this file first to know which log is active
```
```

### 5. Understanding Pipeline Stages (CRITICAL)

**The log does NOT show clear "Stage 1 Complete, Stage 2 Started" messages. You MUST search backwards through the log to understand what stage the pipeline is in.**

**Pipeline has 2 sequential stages:**
1. **Stage 1: PDF Parsing** (8-10 hours) - Extract text and chunks from ALL PDFs
2. **Stage 2: Embedding & Upload** (1-2 hours) - Generate vectors and upload to Qdrant

**To determine current stage, search the log backwards:**

```bash
# Find parsing completion
grep -E "(Extracted content for|Batch.*complete)" /tmp/agent-zot-production-index.log | tail -20

# - "Batch 3400-3426 complete, garbage collected" = parsing FINISHED
# - "add_documents called with XXXX documents" = embedding STARTED
# - "Processing batch X/Y (500 docs)" = embedding in progress
# - "Uploaded batch X" = uploading to Qdrant

#!/bin/bash
# Quick script to check actual indexing status

echo "=== INDEXING STATUS CHECK ==="
echo ""
echo "1. Process check:"
ps aux | grep "agent-zot update-db" | grep -v grep | head -1 | awk '{print "PID: " $2 " | CPU: " $3 "% | Running: " $10 " " $11 " " $12}'
echo ""

echo "2. Active log file (most recent):"
ls -lth /tmp/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -1
echo ""

echo "3. Recent log activity:"
ACTIVE_LOG=$(ls -t /tmp/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -1)
echo "Log: $ACTIVE_LOG"
tail -3 "$ACTIVE_LOG" | grep -E "(Processed|Uploading|batch)" || echo "No recent progress lines"
echo ""

echo "4. Qdrant current count:"
curl -s http://localhost:6333/collections/zotero_library_qdrant 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys, json; data = json.load(sys.stdin); print(f\"Points: {data['result']['points_count']:,}\")" 2>/dev/null || echo "Could not reach Qdrant"
echo ""

echo "=== ALWAYS verify with Qdrant count - logs can lie! ==="
```

## 4. Errors and Fixes

### Error 1: Wrong Log File Confusion (CRITICAL)
**What happened**: User asked "is the indexing still running?" and I checked `/tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log` instead of the active log.

**My incorrect analysis**:
- Concluded process was stuck for 12+ hours
- Showed 0.1% CPU, status SN (sleeping)

**User feedback**: 
- "i dont believe this. just an hour ago you were giving me steady updates saying everything was running smoothly. what happened. are you sure about all this?"

**How I fixed it**:
1. User insisted on checking raw data
2. I ran `ls -lt /tmp/*.log` to find most recently modified log
3. Discovered actual active log: `/tmp/agent-zot-production-index.log` (16 MB, updated 2 min ago)
4. Verified with Qdrant API showing 92,980 chunks
5. Found parsing was 100% complete, embedding was running correctly

**Root cause**: Multiple old log files from previous runs. I grabbed an old one by name pattern instead of checking modification time.

**Prevention implemented**:
- Created `/tmp/ACTIVE_INDEXING_LOG.txt` reference file
- Created `/tmp/check-indexing-status.sh` verification script
- Added 3-step verification protocol to CLAUDE.md
- Archived 30 old log files to `~/agent-zot-logs-archive/`

### Error 2: Incorrect Pipeline Architecture Understanding
**What happened**: I initially explained that parsing and embedding happen in parallel batches.

**User feedback**:
- "are you sure about this?? my understanding was that it first extracts and parses ALL papers and then embeds and vectorizes ALL papers i.e. only after they've been extracted and parsed"

**How I fixed it**:
1. Read `semantic.py:425-508` to verify actual code flow
2. Found loop processes in batches of 200, storing results in `extraction_data` dict
3. Used grep to find parsing completion markers in log
4. Confirmed user was CORRECT: Pipeline is sequential (parse ALL → embed ALL)

**Updated understanding**:
```python
# Process ALL papers first (Stage 1)
for batch_start in range(0, len(local_items), batch_size):
    # Parse 200 papers at a time with 8 workers
    # Store results in extraction_data dict
    
# THEN embed ALL chunks (Stage 2)
# After extraction_data is fully populated
```

**Documentation updated**: Added section 5 to CLAUDE.md explaining sequential pipeline and how to detect stage transitions

   - Include actual timestamps from logs
   - Show both chunk counts AND point counts
   - Calculate percentages
   - Estimate completion time
   - Use emojis consistently

   - Don't report based on Qdrant count alone
   - Don't assume parsing finished without log verification
   - Don't forget to search backwards

   469→
   470→## Critical Fixes
   471→
   472→**Production-ready improvements (October 2025)**
   473→
   474→### 1. Subprocess Isolation
   475→
   476→**Problem**: pypdfium2 C++ backend crashes bypassed Python exception handling, causing semaphore leaks and process crashes after 150-200 PDFs.
   477→
   478→**Solution**: Run Docling in isolated subprocess with configurable timeout.
   479→
   480→**Benefits**:
   481→- ✅ Main process immune to C++ crashes
   482→- ✅ Handles large documents (1-hour timeout)
   483→- ✅ Supports infinite timeout (`null`)
   484→- ✅ Clear error codes: `"failed"`, `"timeout"`, `"error"`
   485→
   486→**Implementation**: `local_db.py:_extract_text_from_pdf()`
   487→
   488→### 2. Removed pdfminer Fallback
   489→
   490→**Problem**: PDFs timing out fell back to pdfminer, resulting in inconsistent output quality:
   491→- Docling: 49 chunks × 512 tokens + rich metadata (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐)
   492→- pdfminer: 1 blob × 8000 tokens, no metadata (⭐⭐)
   493→
   494→**Solution**: Removed pdfminer fallback entirely.
   495→
   496→**Benefits**:
   497→- ✅ 100% consistent high-quality chunking
   498→- ✅ All indexed papers have identical structure
   499→- ✅ Fail loudly instead of silent degradation
   500→
   501→### 3. Configurable Timeout
   502→
   503→**Problem**: 30s timeout insufficient for large documents (textbooks, dissertations).
   504→
   505→**Solution**: Configurable timeout with sensible defaults.
   506→
   507→**Options**:
   508→- `3600` (1 hour) - Default, handles most documents
   509→- `null` - Infinite timeout for extremely large PDFs
   510→- Custom integer - Set per your needs
   511→
   512→**Configuration**: `config.json` → `semantic_search.docling.subprocess_timeout`
   513→

   515→
   516→## Indexing Pipeline
   517→
   518→**Standard default production pipeline command:**
   519→
   520→\```bash
   521→agent-zot update-db --force-rebuild --fulltext
   522→\```
   523→
   524→### What This Does
   525→
   526→**Step-by-step execution:**
   527→
   528→1. ✅ **Delete Qdrant collection** (`--force-rebuild` flag)
   529→   - Ensures clean slate
   530→   - Removes any contaminated data
   531→
   532→2. ✅ **Read all items from local Zotero database**
   533→   - Direct SQLite access (fast)
   534→   - No API rate limits
   535→
   536→3. ✅ **Parse PDFs with Docling**
   537→   - Subprocess-isolated (crash-proof)
   538→   - 1-hour timeout per PDF
   539→   - CPU-only processing (7.3x faster)
   540→   - HybridChunker: 512 tokens per chunk
   541→   - Preserves structure + metadata
   542→
   543→4. ✅ **Generate embeddings**
   544→   - BGE-M3 dense vectors (1024D)
   545→   - BM25 sparse vectors (10,000 features)
   546→   - GPU-accelerated (batch size 32)
   547→
   548→5. ✅ **Store in Qdrant**
   549→   - Hybrid vectors (dense + sparse)
   550→   - Scalar quantization (int8)
   551→   - HNSW indexing (m=32, ef=200)
   552→   - Batch size 500 for fast writes
   553→
   554→6. ✅ **Extract Neo4j knowledge graph** (optional)
   555→   - GPT-4o-mini entity extraction
   556→   - 6 entity types, 10 relationship types
   557→   - Entity resolution enabled
   558→
   559→7. ✅ **Optimize Qdrant collection**
   560→   - Automatic after indexing
   561→   - Builds final HNSW index
   562→
   563→### Command Flags
   564→
   565→| Flag | Effect | Default |
   566→|------|--------|---------|
   567→| `--force-rebuild` | Delete collection before indexing | `false` (incremental) |
   568→| `--fulltext` | Parse PDFs with Docling | `true` (from config) |
   569→| `--limit N` | Process only N items | None (all items) |
   570→
   571→**Note**: Flags override config defaults. Without flags, uses values from `update_config`.

   655→## Troubleshooting

   657→### Qdrant Connection Issues
   658→
   659→\```bash

   669→
   670→### Docling Parsing Errors
   671→
   672→**Low text extraction** → OCR would trigger (but disabled)
   673→- Solution: Verify PDF is not scanned/image-only
   674→- Consider re-OCRing PDF externally first
   675→
   676→**Large PDFs timeout** → Increase subprocess timeout
   677→- Edit: `config.json` → `docling.subprocess_timeout`
   678→- Set to `null` for infinite timeout
   679→
   680→**Formula parsing issues** → Toggle formula enrichment
   681→- Edit: `config.json` → `docling.do_formula_enrichment`
   682→
   683→### Neo4j Issues

   685→\```bash
   686→# Check Neo4j status
   687→docker logs agent-zot-neo4j
   688→
   689→# Access Neo4j browser
   690→open http://localhost:7474
   691→# Login: neo4j / demodemo
   692→\```

   703→
   704→## Active Pipeline Components
   705→
   706→**For the complete, detailed execution path of the production indexing pipeline, see the [Active Pipeline Reference](../CLAUDE.md#active-pipeline-reference) section in CLAUDE.md.**
   707→
   708→This section provides a high-level overview of which files and directories are active in the standard production pipeline:
   709→
   710→### Standard Production Command
   711→
   712→\```bash
   713→agent-zot update-db --force-rebuild --fulltext
   714→\```
   715→
   716→### Active Execution Path
   717→
   718→**Core files used** (in order of execution):
   719→
   720→1. **CLI Entry Point**: `src/agent_zot/core/cli.py`
   721→   - Parses command-line flags
   722→   - Loads config from `~/.config/agent-zot/config.json`
   723→
   724→2. **Orchestration**: `src/agent_zot/search/semantic.py`
   725→   - Routes to appropriate indexing path
   726→   - For fulltext + local mode → delegates to `local_zotero.py`
   727→
   728→3. **Local Database Access** (MAIN ACTIVE PATH): `src/agent_zot/database/local_zotero.py`
   729→   - Direct SQLite access to Zotero database
   730→   - Parallel PDF processing (8 workers)
   731→   - **Contains correct hardcoded defaults** for all Docling settings
   732→   - **This is where the magic happens for production indexing**
   733→
   734→4. **PDF Parsing**: `src/agent_zot/parsers/docling.py`
   735→   - Runs in isolated subprocess (crash protection)
   736→   - HybridChunker with BGE-M3 tokenizer
   737→   - CPU-only processing (7.3x faster than GPU)
   738→
   739→5. **Vector Storage**: `src/agent_zot/clients/qdrant.py`
   740→   - BGE-M3 embedding generation (GPU-accelerated)
   741→   - Hybrid vectors (dense 1024D + sparse BM25)
   742→   - Batch upsert to Qdrant (batch_size=500)
   743→
   744→### Data Locations
   745→
   746→**Active storage locations**:
   747→
   748→| Location | Purpose | Required |
   749→|----------|---------|----------|
   750→| `~/.config/agent-zot/config.json` | User configuration overrides | ✅ Yes |
   751→| `~/Zotero/zotero.sqlite` | Zotero source database | ✅ Yes |
   752→| `~/toolboxes/agent-zot/qdrant_storage/` | Vector data storage | ✅ Yes |
   753→| `/tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log` | Live indexing log | ✅ Yes |
   754→
   755→### Minimal Required Configuration
   756→
   757→**Only 4 settings need to be in `config.json`** - everything else uses smart defaults:
   758→
   759→\```json
   760→{
   761→  "client_env": {
   762→    "ZOTERO_LOCAL": "true"
   763→  },
   764→  "semantic_search": {
   765→    "embedding_model": "sentence-transformers",
   766→    "sentence_transformer_model": "BAAI/bge-m3",
   767→    "collection_name": "zotero_library_qdrant"
   768→  }
   769→}
   770→\```
   771→
   772→All other settings documented in this file (Docling chunking, HNSW parameters, quantization, etc.) have correct hardcoded defaults in `local_zotero.py` and only need to be added to `config.json` if you want to override them.
   773→
   774→### Files NOT in Active Path
   775→
   776→These files exist but are NOT used for the standard production pipeline:
   777→
   778→- ❌ `src/agent_zot/parsers/pymupdf_parser.py` - Deprecated parser
   779→- ❌ `src/agent_zot/clients/chroma_client.py` - Old vector database
   780→- ❌ `src/agent_zot/clients/better_bibtex.py` - Optional, not required
   781→- ❌ `config_examples/config_chroma.json` - Old template
   782→
   783→### Why Two Code Paths?
   784→
   785→**Short answer**: `semantic.py` handles both API mode and local mode. For fulltext + local mode (our standard production pipeline), it delegates to `local_zotero.py` which has optimized parallel processing and correct defaults.
   786→
   787→**Key insight**: The DoclingParser defaults in `semantic.py:77-87` are NOT used for fulltext indexing with local mode. Instead, `local_zotero.py:265-272` provides the correct defaults via subprocess code generation.
   788→
   789→### Verification
   790→
   791→**How to verify the correct pipeline is active**:
   792→
   793→\```bash
   794→# Check config has BGE-M3
   795→grep "sentence_transformer_model" ~/.config/agent-zot/config.json
   796→
   797→# Verify BGE-M3 loading in log
   798→tail -f /tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log | grep "Load pretrained"
   799→# Should show: "BAAI/bge-m3"
   800→
   801→# Verify 1024D vectors
   802→tail -f /tmp/agent-zot-bge-m3-reindex.log | grep "dimension"
   803→# Should show: "dimension: 1024"
   804→
   805→# Check physical storage
   806→du -sh ~/toolboxes/agent-zot/qdrant_storage/collections/zotero_library_qdrant/
   807→\```
   808→
   809→**For complete details on the execution flow, verification points, and troubleshooting, see [CLAUDE.md - Active Pipeline Reference](../CLAUDE.md#active-pipeline-reference).**

## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The user had multiple explicit requests in this conversation:

1. **Configure Neo4j GraphRAG integration** to populate a knowledge graph with text already stored in Qdrant
2. **Ensure NO re-indexing occurs** - critically important that existing Qdrant data (3,087 points from 18-hour indexing) remains untouched
3. **Match configuration.md specifications exactly** - particularly using `ollama/mistral:7b-instruct` instead of GPT-4o-mini
4. **Create backup before proceeding** - User wanted insurance against accidental data loss
5. **Test on small subset first** - Run on 10 papers to verify everything works before processing all 3,087 items

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Neo4j GraphRAG**: Knowledge graph extraction from research papers using LLM
- **Ollama**: Local LLM server for running Mistral 7B Instruct model
- **Mistral 7B Instruct**: Free local LLM model for entity extraction (4.4 GB download)
- **Entity Types**: 8 types (Person, Institution, Concept, Method, Dataset, Theory, Journal, Field)
- **Relationship Types**: 12 types (AUTHORED_BY, AFFILIATED_WITH, USES_METHOD, etc.)
- **Entity Resolution**: Merging similar entities (e.g., "Stanford" = "Stanford University")
- **Lexical Graph**: Keyword connections for full-text search
- **Qdrant Vector Database**: Contains 3,087 points with BGE-M3 (1024D) embeddings
- **Deduplication**: Always-on feature that skips existing points during indexing
- **force_rebuild flag**: When true, triggers collection deletion (line 689-691 in semantic.py)
- **Docling V2 Parser**: CPU-only PDF parsing with subprocess isolation
- **Agent-Zot MCP Server**: Zotero integration via Model Context Protocol

def _add_items_to_graph(self, items: List[Dict[str, Any]], documents: List[str]):
    """
    Add items to Neo4j knowledge graph using batch processing.
    
    Note: We extract full document text from item.data.fulltext instead of using
    the documents parameter, because documents contains chunks not full texts.
    """
    if not self.neo4j_client:
        return
    
    # Prepare papers for batch processing
    papers = []
    for item in items:
        # Extract full document text from item data (where Docling stored it)
        fulltext_data = item_data.get("fulltext", "")
        if isinstance(fulltext_data, dict):
            # Docling format: {"text": "...", "chunks": [...], ...}
            doc_text = fulltext_data.get("text", "")
        else:
            doc_text = fulltext_data if fulltext_data else ""
        
        # Skip if no meaningful text
        if not doc_text or len(doc_text.strip()) < 100:
            logger.debug(f"Skipping Neo4j extraction for {paper_key}: insufficient text")
            continue
```

   321→            logger.warning(f"Error initializing schema (may already exist): {e}")
   322→
   323→    def close(self):
   324→        """Close Neo4j driver connection."""
   325→        if self.driver:
   326→            self.driver.close()
   327→
   328→    def add_paper_to_graph(self,
   329→                          paper_key: str,
   330→                          title: str,
   331→                          abstract: str,
   332→                          authors: List[str],
   333→                          year: Optional[int] = None,
   334→                          chunks: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   335→        """
   336→        Add a research paper to the knowledge graph.
   337→
   338→        Args:
   339→            paper_key: Zotero item key
   340→            title: Paper title
   341→            abstract: Paper abstract
   342→            authors: List of author names
   343→            year: Publication year
   344→            chunks: Optional document chunks from Docling
   345→
   346→        Returns:
   347→            Result of the operation
   348→        """
   349→        try:
   350→            # Build content for entity extraction
   351→            content_parts = [f"Title: {title}"]
   352→
   353→            if authors:
   354→                content_parts.append(f"Authors: {', '.join(authors)}")
   355→
   356→            if year:
   357→                content_parts.append(f"Year: {year}")
   358→
   359→            if abstract:
   360→                content_parts.append(f"\nAbstract: {abstract}")
   361→
   362→            if chunks:
   363→                # Add first few chunks for more context
   364→                content_parts.append("\nKey Content:")
   365→                content_parts.extend(chunks[:3])
   366→
   367→            full_content = "\n\n".join(content_parts)
   368→
   369→            # Create custom extraction template with research-specific prompt
   370→            extraction_template = ERExtractionTemplate(
   371→                template=RESEARCH_EXTRACTION_PROMPT
   372→            )
   373→
   374→            # Configure lexical graph for keyword-based connections
   375→            # Use keyword arguments instead of dict (Pydantic v2 compatibility)
   376→            lexical_config = LexicalGraphConfig(
   377→                chunk_id_property="id",
   378→                chunk_text_property="text",
   379→                chunk_embedding_property="embedding"
   380→            )
   381→
   382→            # Create knowledge graph pipeline with optimized settings
   383→            kg_builder = SimpleKGPipeline(
   384→                llm=self.llm,
   385→                driver=self.driver,
   386→                database=self.neo4j_database,
   387→                embedder=self.embeddings,
   388→                entities=["Person", "Institution", "Concept", "Method", "Dataset", "Theory"],
   389→                relations=["AUTHORED_BY", "AFFILIATED_WITH", "USES_METHOD", "USES_DATASET",
   390→                          "APPLIES_THEORY", "DISCUSSES_CONCEPT", "BUILDS_ON", "EXTENDS",
   391→                          "RELATED_TO", "CITES"],
   392→                potential_schema=RESEARCH_PAPER_SCHEMA + RESEARCH_PAPER_RELATIONS,
   393→                from_pdf=False,
   394→                prompt_template=extraction_template,
   395→                perform_entity_resolution=True,  # Merge similar entities
   396→                lexical_graph_config=lexical_config  # Enable keyword-based connections
   397→            )
   398→
   399→            # Add paper metadata as a node first
   400→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   401→                session.run(
   402→                    """
   403→                    MERGE (p:Paper {item_key: $item_key})
   404→                    SET p.title = $title,
   405→                        p.abstract = $abstract,
   406→                        p.year = $year,
   407→                        p.authors = $authors
   408→                    """,
   409→                    item_key=paper_key,
   410→                    title=title,
   411→                    abstract=abstract,
   412→                    year=year,
   413→                    authors=authors
   414→                )
   415→
   416→            # Extract entities and relationships from content
   417→            result = kg_builder.run_async(text=full_content)
   418→
   419→            # Link extracted entities to the paper
   420→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   421→                session.run(
   422→                    """
   423→                    MATCH (p:Paper {item_key: $item_key})
   424→                    MATCH (e)
   425→                    WHERE e.id IS NOT NULL
   426→                    MERGE (p)-[:MENTIONS]->(e)
   427→                    """,
   428→                    item_key=paper_key
   429→                )
   430→
   431→            logger.info(f"Added paper to graph: {title}")
   432→            return {
   433→                "status": "success",
   434→                "paper_key": paper_key,
   435→                "title": title
   436→            }
   437→
   438→        except Exception as e:
   439→            logger.error(f"Error adding paper to graph: {e}")
   440→            return {
   441→                "status": "error",
   442→                "error": str(e)
   443→            }
   444→
   445→    def add_papers_batch(self,
   446→                        papers: List[Dict[str, Any]],
   447→                        batch_size: int = 10) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   448→        """
   449→        Add multiple papers to the knowledge graph in batches.
   450→
   451→        Args:
   452→            papers: List of paper dictionaries with keys:
   453→                   - paper_key, title, abstract, authors, year, chunks (optional)
   454→            batch_size: Number of papers to process in parallel (default: 10)
   455→
   456→        Returns:
   457→            Dictionary with success/failure counts and details
   458→        """
   459→        results = {
   460→            "total": len(papers),
   461→            "successful": 0,
   462→            "failed": 0,
   463→            "errors": []
   464→        }
   465→
   466→        try:
   467→            # Process papers in batches
   468→            for i in range(0, len(papers), batch_size):
   469→                batch = papers[i:i + batch_size]
   470→                logger.info(f"Processing batch {i//batch_size + 1}/{(len(papers) + batch_size - 1)//batch_size} ({len(batch)} papers)")
   471→
   472→                # Build combined content for batch
   473→                batch_content_parts = []
   474→                for paper in batch:
   475→                    content_parts = [f"Title: {paper['title']}"]
   476→
   477→                    if paper.get('authors'):
   478→                        content_parts.append(f"Authors: {', '.join(paper['authors'])}")
   479→                    if paper.get('year'):
   480→                        content_parts.append(f"Year: {paper['year']}")
   481→                    if paper.get('abstract'):
   482→                        content_parts.append(f"\nAbstract: {paper['abstract']}")
   483→                    if paper.get('chunks'):
   484→                        content_parts.append("\nKey Content:")
   485→                        content_parts.extend(paper['chunks'][:2])  # Fewer chunks per paper in batch
   486→
   487→                    batch_content_parts.append("\n\n=== PAPER ===\n\n" + "\n\n".join(content_parts))
   488→
   489→                batch_content = "\n\n---\n\n".join(batch_content_parts)
   490→
   491→                # Create extraction template
   492→                extraction_template = ERExtractionTemplate(template=RESEARCH_EXTRACTION_PROMPT)
   493→                lexical_config = LexicalGraphConfig({
   494→                    "id": "__Entity__",
   495→                    "label": "__Entity__",
   496→                    "text": "text",
   497→                    "embedding": "embedding"
   498→                })
   499→
   500→                # Create pipeline for batch
   501→                kg_builder = SimpleKGPipeline(
   502→                    llm=self.llm,
   503→                    driver=self.driver,
   504→                    database=self.neo4j_database,
   505→                    embedder=self.embeddings,
   506→                    entities=["Person", "Institution", "Concept", "Method", "Dataset", "Theory"],
   507→                    relations=["AUTHORED_BY", "AFFILIATED_WITH", "USES_METHOD", "USES_DATASET",
   508→                              "APPLIES_THEORY", "DISCUSSES_CONCEPT", "BUILDS_ON", "EXTENDS",
   509→                              "RELATED_TO", "CITES"],
   510→                    potential_schema=RESEARCH_PAPER_SCHEMA + RESEARCH_PAPER_RELATIONS,
   511→                    from_pdf=False,
   512→                    prompt_template=extraction_template,
   513→                    perform_entity_resolution=True,
   514→                    lexical_graph_config=lexical_config
   515→                )
   516→
   517→                # Add paper metadata nodes for batch
   518→                with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   519→                    for paper in batch:
   520→                        try:
   521→                            session.run(
   522→                                """
   523→                                MERGE (p:Paper {item_key: $item_key})
   524→                                SET p.title = $title,
   525→                                    p.abstract = $abstract,
   526→                                    p.year = $year,
   527→                                    p.authors = $authors
   528→                                """,
   529→                                item_key=paper['paper_key'],
   530→                                title=paper['title'],
   531→                                abstract=paper.get('abstract', ''),
   532→                                year=paper.get('year'),
   533→                                authors=paper.get('authors', [])
   534→                            )
   535→                        except Exception as e:
   536→                            logger.error(f"Error adding paper metadata for {paper['paper_key']}: {e}")
   537→                            results["failed"] += 1
   538→                            results["errors"].append({"paper_key": paper['paper_key'], "error": str(e)})
   539→                            continue
   540→
   541→                # Extract entities from batch content
   542→                try:
   543→                    kg_builder.run_async(text=batch_content)
   544→
   545→                    # Link extracted entities to papers
   546→                    with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   547→                        for paper in batch:
   548→                            try:
   549→                                session.run(
   550→                                    """
   551→                                    MATCH (p:Paper {item_key: $item_key})
   552→                                    MATCH (e)
   553→                                    WHERE e.id IS NOT NULL
   554→                                    MERGE (p)-[:MENTIONS]->(e)
   555→                                    """,
   556→                                    item_key=paper['paper_key']
   557→                                )
   558→                                results["successful"] += 1
   559→                                logger.info(f"Successfully added paper: {paper['title']}")
   560→                            except Exception as e:
   561→                                logger.error(f"Error linking entities for {paper['paper_key']}: {e}")
   562→                                results["failed"] += 1
   563→                                results["errors"].append({"paper_key": paper['paper_key'], "error": str(e)})
   564→
   565→                except Exception as e:
   566→                    logger.error(f"Error processing batch: {e}")
   567→                    for paper in batch:
   568→                        results["failed"] += 1
   569→                        results["errors"].append({"paper_key": paper['paper_key'], "error": f"Batch error: {str(e)}"})
   570→
   571→            logger.info(f"Batch processing complete: {results['successful']}/{results['total']} successful")
   572→            return results
   573→
   574→        except Exception as e:
   575→            logger.error(f"Fatal error in batch processing: {e}")
   576→            return {
   577→                "status": "error",
   578→                "error": str(e),
   579→                **results
   580→            }
   581→
   582→    def search_entities(self,
   583→                       query: str,
   584→                       entity_types: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   585→                       limit: int = 10) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   586→        """
   587→        Search for entities in the knowledge graph.
   588→
   589→        Args:
   590→            query: Search query
   591→            entity_types: Filter by entity types (e.g., ["Concept", "Method"])
   592→            limit: Maximum number of results
   593→
   594→        Returns:
   595→            List of matching entities with their properties
   596→        """
   597→        try:
   598→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   599→                # Build entity type filter
   600→                type_filter = ""
   601→                if entity_types:
   602→                    labels = " OR ".join([f"e:{t}" for t in entity_types])
   603→                    type_filter = f"WHERE {labels}"
   604→
   605→                # Search using text match
   606→                cypher_query = f"""
   607→                MATCH (e)
   608→                {type_filter}
   609→                WHERE toLower(e.name) CONTAINS toLower($query)
   610→                   OR toLower(e.description) CONTAINS toLower($query)
   611→                RETURN e, labels(e) as types
   612→                LIMIT $limit
   613→                """
   614→
   615→                result = session.run(cypher_query, query=query, limit=limit)
   616→
   617→                entities = []
   618→                for record in result:
   619→                    entity = dict(record["e"])
   620→                    entity["types"] = record["types"]
   621→                    entities.append(entity)
   622→
   623→                logger.info(f"Found {len(entities)} entities matching: {query}")
   624→                return entities
   625→
   626→        except Exception as e:
   627→            logger.error(f"Error searching entities: {e}")
   628→            return []
   629→
   630→    def find_related_papers(self,
   631→                           paper_key: str,
   632→                           max_depth: int = 2,
   633→                           limit: int = 10) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   634→        """
   635→        Find papers related to a given paper via shared entities.
   636→
   637→        Args:
   638→            paper_key: Zotero item key of the source paper
   639→            max_depth: Maximum graph traversal depth
   640→            limit: Maximum number of results
   641→
   642→        Returns:
   643→            List of related papers with relationship information
   644→        """
   645→        try:
   646→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   647→                cypher_query = """
   648→                MATCH (source:Paper {item_key: $paper_key})
   649→                MATCH path = (source)-[:MENTIONS*1..2]-(entity)-[:MENTIONS*1..2]-(related:Paper)
   650→                WHERE source <> related
   651→                WITH related,
   652→                     count(DISTINCT entity) as shared_entities,
   653→                     collect(DISTINCT entity.name)[0..5] as sample_entities
   654→                RETURN related.item_key as item_key,
   655→                       related.title as title,
   656→                       related.year as year,
   657→                       related.authors as authors,
   658→                       shared_entities,
   659→                       sample_entities
   660→                ORDER BY shared_entities DESC
   661→                LIMIT $limit
   662→                """
   663→
   664→                result = session.run(
   665→                    cypher_query,
   666→                    paper_key=paper_key,
   667→                    limit=limit
   668→                )
   669→
   670→                related_papers = []
   671→                for record in result:
   672→                    related_papers.append({
   673→                        "item_key": record["item_key"],
   674→                        "title": record["title"],
   675→                        "year": record["year"],
   676→                        "authors": record["authors"],
   677→                        "shared_entities": record["shared_entities"],
   678→                        "sample_entities": record["sample_entities"]
   679→                    })
   680→
   681→                logger.info(f"Found {len(related_papers)} related papers for: {paper_key}")
   682→                return related_papers
   683→
   684→        except Exception as e:
   685→            logger.error(f"Error finding related papers: {e}")
   686→            return []
   687→
   688→    def find_citation_chain(self, paper_key: str, max_hops: int = 2, limit: int = 10) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   689→        """
   690→        Find papers citing papers that cite the given paper (multi-hop citation analysis).
   691→
   692→        Args:
   693→            paper_key: Zotero item key of the starting paper
   694→            max_hops: Maximum number of citation hops (default: 2)
   695→            limit: Maximum number of papers to return per hop (default: 10)
   696→
   697→        Returns:
   698→            List of papers with citation hop distance and paths
   699→        """
   700→        try:
   701→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   702→                # Cypher query for multi-hop citation traversal
   703→                query = """
   704→                MATCH path = (start:Paper {item_key: $paper_key})-[:CITES*1..%d]-(cited:Paper)
   705→                WHERE start <> cited
   706→                RETURN DISTINCT cited.item_key as item_key,
   707→                       cited.title as title,
   708→                       cited.year as year,
   709→                       length(path) as hops,
   710→                       [node in nodes(path) | node.title] as path_titles
   711→                ORDER BY hops ASC, cited.year DESC
   712→                LIMIT $limit
   713→                """ % max_hops
   714→
   715→                result = session.run(query, paper_key=paper_key, limit=limit)
   716→
   717→                citation_chain = []
   718→                for record in result:
   719→                    citation_chain.append({
   720→                        "item_key": record["item_key"],
   721→                        "title": record["title"],
   722→                        "year": record["year"],
   723→                        "citation_hops": record["hops"],
   724→                        "citation_path": record["path_titles"]
   725→                    })
   726→
   727→                logger.info(f"Found {len(citation_chain)} papers in citation chain for: {paper_key}")
   728→                return citation_chain
   729→
   730→        except Exception as e:
   731→            logger.error(f"Error finding citation chain: {e}")
   732→            return []
   733→
   734→    def find_related_concepts(self, concept: str, max_hops: int = 2, limit: int = 15) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   735→        """
   736→        Find concepts related through intermediate concepts (concept propagation).
   737→
   738→        Args:
   739→            concept: Starting concept name
   740→            max_hops: Maximum number of concept relationship hops (default: 2)
   741→            limit: Maximum number of related concepts to return (default: 15)
   742→
   743→        Returns:
   744→            List of related concepts with relationship paths
   745→        """
   746→        try:
   747→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   748→                # Find concepts related through DISCUSSES_CONCEPT relationships
   749→                query = """
   750→                MATCH path = (start:Concept {name: $concept})<-[:DISCUSSES_CONCEPT*1..%d]-(p:Paper)-[:DISCUSSES_CONCEPT]->(related:Concept)
   751→                WHERE start <> related
   752→                WITH related, collect(DISTINCT p.title) as papers, length(path) as hops
   753→                RETURN DISTINCT related.name as concept_name,
   754→                       hops,
   755→                       papers[0..3] as sample_papers,
   756→                       size(papers) as paper_count
   757→                ORDER BY paper_count DESC, hops ASC
   758→                LIMIT $limit
   759→                """ % max_hops
   760→
   761→                result = session.run(query, concept=concept, limit=limit)
   762→
   763→                related_concepts = []
   764→                for record in result:
   765→                    related_concepts.append({
   766→                        "concept": record["concept_name"],
   767→                        "relationship_hops": record["hops"],
   768→                        "paper_count": record["paper_count"],
   769→                        "sample_papers": record["sample_papers"]
   770→                    })
   771→
   772→                logger.info(f"Found {len(related_concepts)} related concepts for: {concept}")
   773→                return related_concepts
   774→
   775→        except Exception as e:
   776→            logger.error(f"Error finding related concepts: {e}")
   777→            return []
   778→
   779→    def find_collaborator_network(self, author: str, max_hops: int = 2, limit: int = 20) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   780→        """
   781→        Find collaborators of collaborators (co-authorship network).
   782→
   783→        Args:
   784→            author: Author name to start from
   785→            max_hops: Maximum number of collaboration hops (default: 2)
   786→            limit: Maximum number of collaborators to return (default: 20)
   787→
   788→        Returns:
   789→            List of authors with collaboration distance and shared papers
   790→        """
   791→        try:
   792→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   793→                # Find collaborators through co-authorship
   794→                query = """
   795→                MATCH path = (start:Person {name: $author})<-[:AUTHORED_BY*1..%d]-(p:Paper)-[:AUTHORED_BY]->(collab:Person)
   796→                WHERE start <> collab
   797→                WITH collab, collect(DISTINCT p.title) as papers, length(path) as hops
   798→                RETURN DISTINCT collab.name as author_name,
   799→                       hops,
   800→                       papers[0..3] as sample_papers,
   801→                       size(papers) as collaboration_count
   802→                ORDER BY collaboration_count DESC, hops ASC
   803→                LIMIT $limit
   804→                """ % max_hops
   805→
   806→                result = session.run(query, author=author, limit=limit)
   807→
   808→                collaborators = []
   809→                for record in result:
   810→                    collaborators.append({
   811→                        "author": record["author_name"],
   812→                        "collaboration_hops": record["hops"],
   813→                        "collaboration_count": record["collaboration_count"],
   814→                        "sample_papers": record["sample_papers"]
   815→                    })
   816→
   817→                logger.info(f"Found {len(collaborators)} collaborators for: {author}")
   818→                return collaborators
   819→
   820→        except Exception as e:
   821→            logger.error(f"Error finding collaborator network: {e}")
   822→            return []
   823→
   824→    def find_seminal_papers(self, field: str = None, top_n: int = 10) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   825→        """
   826→        Find most influential papers using PageRank algorithm on citation graph.
   827→
   828→        Args:
   829→            field: Optional field name to filter papers (default: None, all fields)
   830→            top_n: Number of top papers to return (default: 10)
   831→
   832→        Returns:
   833→            List of papers ranked by influence (PageRank score)
   834→        """
   835→        try:
   836→            with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   837→                # Build query with optional field filter
   838→                if field:
   839→                    # Filter by field if specified
   840→                    query = """
   841→                    CALL gds.graph.project(
   842→                        'citationGraph',
   843→                        'Paper',
   844→                        {
   845→                            CITES: {
   846→                                orientation: 'REVERSE'
   847→                            }
   848→                        }
   849→                    )
   850→                    YIELD graphName
   851→
   852→                    CALL gds.pageRank.stream('citationGraph')
   853→                    YIELD nodeId, score
   854→                    WITH gds.util.asNode(nodeId) AS paper, score
   855→                    WHERE EXISTS {
   856→                        MATCH (paper)-[:BELONGS_TO_FIELD]->(f:Field {name: $field})
   857→                    }
   858→                    RETURN paper.item_key as item_key,
   859→                           paper.title as title,
   860→                           paper.year as year,
   861→                           score
   862→                    ORDER BY score DESC
   863→                    LIMIT $top_n
   864→                    """
   865→                    # Note: This is a simplified version. In production, you'd want to:
   866→                    # 1. Check if graph exists before projecting
   867→                    # 2. Drop graph after use
   868→                    # 3. Use gds.graph.exists() to avoid re-creating
   869→                else:
   870→                    # All papers PageRank
   871→                    query = """
   872→                    MATCH (p:Paper)
   873→                    WITH p, size([(p)<-[:CITES]-() | 1]) as citation_count
   874→                    RETURN p.item_key as item_key,
   875→                           p.title as title,
   876→                           p.year as year,
   877→                           citation_count as score
   878→                    ORDER BY score DESC
   879→                    LIMIT $top_n
   880→                    """
   881→                    # Simplified version using citation count as proxy for PageRank
   882→                    # Full GDS PageRank requires Neo4j Graph Data Science library
   883→
   884→                params = {"top_n": top_n}
   885→                if field:
   886→                    params["field"] = field
   887→
   888→                result = session.run(query, **params)
   889→
   890→                seminal_papers = []
   891→                for record in result:
   892→                    seminal_papers.append({
   893→                        "item_key": record["item_key"],
   894→                        "title": record["title"],
   895→                        "year": record["year"],
   896→                        "influence_score": float(record["score"])
   897→                    })
   898→
   899→                logger.info(f"Found {len(seminal_papers)} seminal papers" + (f" in field: {field}" if field else ""))
   900→                return seminal_papers
   901→
   902→        except Exception as e:
   903→            logger.error(f"Error finding seminal papers: {e}")
   904→            # Fallback to simple citation count if GDS not available
   905→            logger.info("Falling back to citation count ranking")
   906→            try:
   907→                with self.driver.session(database=self.neo4j_database) as session:
   908→                    fallback_query = """
   909→                    MATCH (p:Paper)
   910→                    WITH p, size([(p)<-[:CITES]-() | 1]) as citation_count
   911→                    WHERE citation_count > 0
   912→                    RETURN p.item_key as item_key,
   913→                           p.title as title,
   914→                           p.year as year,
   915→                           citation_count as score
   916→                    ORDER BY score DESC
   917→                    LIMIT $top_n
   918→                    """
   919→                    result = session.run(fallback_query, top_n=top_n)
   920→
   921→                    seminal_papers = []
   922→                    for record in result:
   923→                        seminal_papers.append({
   924→                            "item_key": record["item_key"],
   925→                            "title": record["title"],
   926→                            "year": record["year"],
   927→                            "influence_score": float(record["score"])
   928→                        })
   929→                    return seminal_papers
   930→            except Exception as fallback_error:
   931→                logger.error(f"Fallback query also failed: {fallback_error}")
   932→                return []
